一.note: As a part: a floor, a lid, or the ground.

丿.note: A stroke falling to the left, like katakana ノ.

乙.note: A bent, hooked stroke. The second stroke of 九 counts as one.

亠.note: A dot on a line: a pot lid, or a top hat.

人.note: On the left it shrinks to 亻; on top it spreads out into a roof or lid.

亻.note: 人 squeezed onto the left side of a character.

儿.note: A pair of walking legs. Always at the bottom.

入.note: Not 人: in 入 the right stroke starts higher and the left one leans in.

八.note: Two strokes parting. As a part it means split or divide.

丷.note: 八 squeezed small to sit on top of something.

冂.note: Three sides of a box, open at the bottom.

冖.note: A flat cover, shaped like katakana ワ.

刀.note: On the right of a character it stands upright as 刂.

刂.note: 刀, sword, standing upright on the right side.

千.note: Not 午, noon, which has one more bar.

卜.note: The crack a fortune-teller read in a heated bone.

口.note: A small square: a mouth, an opening, or simply a box.

囗.note: A big square wrapped round the whole character: a fence, borders. Bigger than 口.

土.note: The lower bar is the longer one. With the upper bar longer it is 士, samurai.

夕.note: A crescent moon just coming up: evening.

大.note: A person with arms flung wide.

女.note: On the left it narrows into おんなへん.

工.note: A tool for ruling straight lines: work, craft.

干.note: A pole with a crossbar. Dictionaries file 年 under it, though it is hard to see there.

幺.note: A tiny twisted thread: small, faint.

彳.note: The left half of 行, go: a person stepping out.

日.note: Narrower and taller than 曰, say.

曰.note: Wider and flatter than 日: a mouth with words coming out.

月.note: Inside many kanji it stands for flesh or the body, not the moon.

木.note: On the left it narrows and its last stroke shortens to a flick, as in 校.

毋.note: The radical 母 and 毎 are filed under.

气.note: Wisps of vapour: air, gas, spirit.

水.note: On the left it becomes three drops, 氵, as in 海 and 泳.

火.note: At the bottom it becomes four dots, 灬.

田.note: A field divided into four paddies.

聿.note: A hand gripping a writing brush.

行.note: A crossroads. Split down the middle, it wraps around other parts.

襾.note: A lid pressed down over something. Dictionaries file 西 under it.

言.note: On the left it becomes ごんべん, the speech radical: 話, 読, 語.

金.note: On the left it becomes かねへん, the metal radical.

門.note: Two swinging doors, wrapped round whatever is inside.

雨.note: On top it flattens into あめかんむり, the weather radical: 電, 雪, 雲.

凵.note: A container open at the top.

又.note: A right hand, seen from the side.

ナ.note: Written like katakana ナ: the hand in 左, 右 and 友.

乂.note: An X made of two strokes.

メ.note: Written like katakana メ. In 気 it replaced 米, rice, when the character was simplified.

寺.note: Earth (土) over a measure (寸). Read ジ, a sound it lends to 時.

交.note: Read コウ, a sound it lends to 校.

玉.note: A king (王) with a dot: his jewel.

可.note: Read カ, a sound it lends to 何.

五.note: Over a mouth (口) it makes 吾, read ゴ — the sound of 語.

⺍.note: Three short strokes on top, like katakana ツ.

母.note: With a stroke on top it becomes 毎, every.

一.mnemonic: One finger laid flat: a single stroke is one. Inside other kanji it often marks the ground, a floor, or a lid.

二.mnemonic: Two lines, two. The lower one is longer, so the pair sits steady.

三.mnemonic: Three lines, three. As in 二, the bottom line is the longest: a stack built to stand.

四.mnemonic: A box (囗) with a pair of legs (儿) trapped inside, kicking at its four walls: four.

五.mnemonic: Think of a boxy 5: a flat top, a stroke down and round into a belly, and a floor to stand on.

六.mnemonic: A dancer in a top hat (亠), legs kicked wide apart (八), counting out a six-step routine.

七.mnemonic: Turn it upside down and it looks like a 7.

八.mnemonic: Two strokes spreading apart, like a pair of doors swinging open. Inside other kanji it keeps that sense — split, divide — as in 分.

九.mnemonic: Nine is one short of ten: picture 十 slumped over, its arm hooked like a runner one step from the finish.

十.mnemonic: A plus sign: add up all your fingers and you get ten.

百.mnemonic: One (一) over white (白): a single silver-white hundred-yen coin. 白 lends its sound too — ハク, ヒャク.

千.mnemonic: Ten (十) with a slash (丿) on top: every slash adds two more zeros — a thousand.

万.mnemonic: A lid (一) over a shape like katakana カ: ka-ching — ten thousand yen, the note in your wallet (一万円).

円.mnemonic: A cash drawer (冂) with a divider down the middle: where the yen go. It also means round, like a coin.

半.mnemonic: Divide (丷) on top, then one cut (丨) straight down through two bars (二): half. It began as an ox split down the middle.

日.mnemonic: Once a picture of the sun: a circle with a dot in it, squared off by the brush. Sun, and so day.

月.mnemonic: Once a picture of a crescent moon, stood upright, with two lines of shadow across it. One turn of the moon is a month.

年.mnemonic: A farmer bent under the harvest: the slanted top is their head, the long stroke a pole running straight down through the sheaves. One harvest, one year.

時.mnemonic: Sun (日) + temple (寺): temple bells rang out the hours by the sun. 寺 is read ジ, and so is 時.

分.mnemonic: Divide (八) with a sword (刀): cut into parts. An hour cut into parts gives minutes.

人.mnemonic: Once a picture of a person seen from the side, striding: two legs. On the left of other kanji it shrinks to 亻.

男.mnemonic: Rice field (田) + power (力): the strength working the field — man, in the old farming picture behind the word.

女.mnemonic: Once a picture of a woman kneeling with her arms crossed in front of her.

子.mnemonic: Once a picture of a swaddled baby: a head on top, arms stretched out wide, and the body wrapped into one hooked stroke.

名.mnemonic: Evening (夕) + mouth (口): in the dark nobody can see who you are, so you call out your name.

父.mnemonic: Crossed sticks (乂) with two chips flying off the top (八): father chopping the firewood.

母.mnemonic: It grew out of 女, woman: bent into a frame, with two dots added for a mother nursing her child.

友.mnemonic: Two hands — one written like ナ, the other 又 — clasped together: friends.

先.mnemonic: Legs (儿) at the bottom and a foot stepping forward on top: going ahead. Whoever went ahead of you is your teacher, 先生.

生.mnemonic: Once a picture of a shoot pushing up out of the earth (土), sprouting leaves: life, birth — and, for food, raw.

天.mnemonic: A line (一) over a big person (大): what lies above even the biggest person — the sky, heaven.

気.mnemonic: Steam (气) rising off a pot of rice, the メ standing in for the grains: breath, spirit, the mind.

雨.mnemonic: Once a picture of rain: the sky along the top, clouds hanging down (冂), and four drops falling. On top of other kanji it means weather, as in 電.

山.mnemonic: Once a picture of three peaks, the middle one tallest: a mountain.

川.mnemonic: Once a picture of water flowing between two banks: a river.

火.mnemonic: Once a picture of flames leaping up, with a spark flying off each side: fire.

水.mnemonic: Once a picture of flowing water: a stream down the middle, splashing off to both sides.

木.mnemonic: Once a picture of a tree: branches across the top, a trunk straight down, and two roots spreading out below.

金.mnemonic: Under a wide roof (人), two nuggets glint in the earth (土): gold, and so money.

土.mnemonic: A mound of earth on the ground, a stake driven into it: earth, soil. The bottom bar is the longer one — longer on top would be 士, samurai.

曜.mnemonic: The sun (日) and a bird (隹) with its wings (羽) spread: the sun, the moon and the planets flying across the sky one after another, each lending its name to a day of the week.

大.mnemonic: A person (人) flinging their arms out wide (一) to show you: "this big!"

小.mnemonic: A hook with a little drop on either side, like crumbs chipped off: small.

中.mnemonic: A stick (丨) through the middle of a box (口): middle, inside.

上.mnemonic: The ground (一) with a stalk and a flag pointing up above it: above, up.

下.mnemonic: The ground (一) with a stalk hanging down beneath it: below, down. It is 上 turned upside down.

東.mnemonic: The sun (日) rising behind a tree (木): east.

西.mnemonic: Once a picture of a bird settling into its nest. Birds go home to roost as the sun sets in the west.

南.mnemonic: A cross (十) on the roof of a big frame (冂) packed with sheaves of grain: the warm south, where the harvest is rich.

北.mnemonic: Once a picture of two people back to back — 匕 on the right, its mirror on the left — turned away from the cold north wind.

外.mnemonic: Evening (夕) + divining rod (卜): the fortune-teller who works at night sets up outside the town walls.

行.mnemonic: Once a picture of a crossroads, drawn here as its left half (彳) and right half (亍): where you go from.

来.mnemonic: A tree (木) heavy with ears of grain (丷): wheat, the crop said to have come down from heaven — come.

出.mnemonic: Two mountains (山) stacked one on the other: to get out, you climb over both.

入.mnemonic: Something ducking in head first: the left stroke leans into the right. Enter. Unlike 人, the right stroke starts higher.

車.mnemonic: Once a picture of a cart seen from above: the box in the middle is its body, the long line through it the axle, a wheel at each end.

前.mnemonic: Horns (丷) over the table, then meat (月) and a knife (刂): the butcher carves the joint right in front of you.

後.mnemonic: A traveller (彳) held back by a thread (幺), on dragging legs (夂): lagging behind — after, behind.

左.mnemonic: A hand (ナ) holding a carpenter's square (工): the left hand holds the tool steady. Written flat stroke first, unlike 右.

右.mnemonic: A hand (ナ) lifting food to the mouth (口): the right hand, the one you eat with. Written slanted stroke first, unlike 左.

間.mnemonic: Sunlight (日) shining through the gap between the doors of a gate (門): the space between.

見.mnemonic: An eye (目) on legs (儿): an eye that walks about looking — see.

聞.mnemonic: An ear (耳) pressed to the gate (門): listening in. Dictionaries file it under the ear, not the gate.

読.mnemonic: Words (言) + sell (売): a market seller calling out their wares — reading aloud.

書.mnemonic: A hand gripping a brush (聿) above a mouth that speaks (曰): writing down what is said.

学.mnemonic: A child (子) under a roof (冖), sparks of knowledge (⺍) flying above their head: study.

校.mnemonic: Wood (木) + mix (交): the wooden building where children mix — school. 交 is read コウ, and so is 校.

語.mnemonic: Words (言), five (五), mouth (口): five mouths speaking words — a language. Five over mouth, 吾, is read ゴ, and so is 語.

本.mnemonic: A tree (木) with a line (一) marking its root: the origin of something — and a book, the root of knowledge.

国.mnemonic: A jewel (玉) — the king's treasure — kept safe inside the borders (囗): a country.

食.mnemonic: A lid (人) over a pot of something good (良): eat, food.

休.mnemonic: A person (亻) leaning against a tree (木): rest.

毎.mnemonic: Mother (母) with a hairpin on top: she puts it in every morning without fail — every.

今.mnemonic: A lid (人) snaps shut over one (一) thing caught on a hook: trapped at this very moment — now.

何.mnemonic: A person (亻) asking "is it possible (可)?" — what? 可 is read カ, and so is 何.

高.mnemonic: Once a picture of a tall tower: a spire (亠), a window (口), and walls (冂) with a door at the bottom — tall, high.

長.mnemonic: Once a picture of an old man with long flowing hair and a walking stick: long — and the eldest is the chief.

白.mnemonic: A ray of light (丿) glinting off the sun (日): white.

午.mnemonic: Thousand (千) with one more bar across it: noon, the top of the day. Easy to confuse — count the bars.

電.mnemonic: Rain (雨, flattened on top) over a bolt of lightning with a hooked tail: electricity, first seen in a storm.
